label: nyiso 72 netrev margin
definition: NYISO KEEPER (owner override 2026-07-23, rule 1 structural fidelity). MARGIN arm of the gas-offer net-revenue margin charter (docs/handoffs/gas-offer-net-revenue-margin-design-2026-07.md; NEISO keeper neiso-61 precedent) — single delta gas_offer_margin=true over the nyiso-70 keeper recipe. Each registered gas band's markup above its MEASURED physical basis (phys_* keys = CAMPD marginal-HR nyiso_campd_marginal_hr_summary.csv p50s) is repriced from fuel-scaled to a fixed $/MWh net-revenue margin at the 3.9046 $/MMBtu train-window delivered-gas anchor; offers reduce EXACTLY to the registered multipliers at anchor gas (zero fitted scalars — only the markup gas-elasticity 1->0). 404-412 gas tranches compressed (median fixed margin 6.04 $/MWh). PRE-REGISTERED REFUTATION NOT MET, RECORDED NOT HIDDEN: the charter bar is 'MARGIN C3b <= BASE C3b every year' and NYISO FAILS it — price duration-shape NRMSE (probe netrev_margin_ab.py, RT) DEGRADES all three years (2023 0.5086->0.5260, 2024 0.3573->0.3781, 2025 0.6155->0.6385). C3a mean: 2023 +18.1%->+20.6% (already out of band; below-anchor firm), 2024 +1.0%->+3.6%, 2025 +5.5%->+1.7% (above-anchor compression, improves). Two-sided mechanism works as designed but is the wrong direction for NYISO's in-sample residual (dominant miss is the 2023 energy-LEVEL gap, not the offer form; same class as CAISO, whose A/B caiso-112 also degraded on 2/3 years). CONSISTENT WITH THE FINAL CAISO DECISION: CAISO was ADOPTED the same day on the same owner directive / rule 1 (keeper 2026-07-23-caiso-netrev-margin-keeper) — the net-revenue margin is the go-forward offer form across ISOs. Kept on the structural-form argument + expected out-of-sample generalization advantage (UNTESTED for NYISO; 2022 holdout not touched — no calibration-complete marker). NO residual tuning taken (rule 1). BASE arm reproduces nyiso-70 byte-identically (maxDelta 0.0000). Fuel-mix/volume unchanged. DETERMINATION NOT-YET (as was nyiso-70), deciding criteria the unchanged 2023 C3a/C3b/C3c energy-LEVEL misses.
market_story: The margin form does not change WHICH plants run — it changes how each gas band's offer tracks the fuel price. Real NYISO gas bidders set their start/no-load hurdle and competitive-reach markup as a $/MWh net-revenue target and hold it as delivered gas moves, rather than scaling the markup up and down with the fuel bill (the multiplicative form). CC_REGULAR / CC_CHP (the marginal downstate/upstate combined-cycle fleet, ~33/13 TWh): committed and econ bands offer their measured physical burn at full delivered gas plus a fixed competitive margin; below the 3.90 anchor (2023/2024) that firms their offer slightly, above it (2025) it compresses toward the physical cost — matching how a CC bids into a soft vs tight gas market. CT_PEAKER (~2 TWh, downstate ramp/scarcity): the 4.0x $-cap peak rung becomes a fixed ~$300/MWh scarcity-margin add rather than a fuel-scaled wall, the $ form of an energy-cap offer. ST_GAS (~7-11 TWh, older downstate steam): the small within-family reshuffle (-0.4..-0.5 TWh) is these units offering a fuel-invariant margin and being marginally out-competed by the CC fleet at below-anchor gas. No class is floor-forced by this mechanism; it is an offer-curve reprice, not a dispatch floor.
